answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a work-weighted stamp ledger: each agent identity must burn a scarce mining resource to earn a plume of verified output, and standing is granted per unit of real computation, not per wallet. Because a new account pays the same copper-priced overhead as any incumbent, splitting one operator across a thousand addresses buys no extra influence, only a thousand bills. A quartz-throttled proof round additionally demands independent timing and peer attestation, so a farm cloning identities pays full cost per head while its vote stays flat.
